title: Embeddings — Compare Directions, Not Just Size
key_insight: Cosine similarity measures the angle between vectors. Dot product mixes direction and length, while Euclidean distance measures straight-line separation.
body:
## Compare Directions, Not Just Size

Two vectors point in nearly the same direction but have different lengths. Their pattern may be more important than their magnitude.

Cosine similarity measures the angle between vectors. Dot product mixes direction and length, while Euclidean distance measures straight-line separation.

Normalize vectors when the retrieval method expects it. The index metric and the model’s training objective should agree.
common_mistakes: An embedding is always a readable paragraph.
Vector closeness proves two statements are factually true.
Every similarity metric ranks all vectors identically.

real_world_usage: Embeddings connect text, images, and users to search, recommendation, retrieval, and neural computation.
explain_back_prompt: Using “Compare Directions, Not Just Size,” explain Embeddings without assuming the listener knows modern AI.
